title: WarpDrive: GPU-Based Fully Homomorphic Encryption Acceleration Leveraging Tensor and CUDA Cores
problem: GPU-based acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is bottlenecked by frequent pipeline stalls from memory-latency-bound Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) operations and by suboptimal utilization of GPU hardware units, leaving both CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores underused for FHE workloads.
motivation: FHE is increasingly important for privacy-preserving computation, but its multi-orders-of-magnitude overhead over plaintext computation demands practical GPU acceleration; existing GPU solutions fail to fully exploit the available parallelism and memory hierarchy of modern NVIDIA GPUs.
method: WarpDrive applies three key optimizations: (1) computation decomposition of NTT that reduces total instruction count by 73% through arithmetic restructuring; (2) fine-grained memory access design that pipelines loads to eliminate 86% of pipeline stalls; (3) a concurrent-execution framework that runs CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores simultaneously within a single NTT kernel — the first such combined use — exploiting both unit types' complementary throughput characteristics. Additionally, intra-ciphertext parallelism is maximally extracted without requiring ciphertext batching.
key_novelty: First framework to concurrently utilize CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores within the same NTT kernel for FHE, exceeding the throughput of either unit type alone.
contributions: Computation decomposition reducing FHE NTT instruction count by 73%.
Fine-grained memory access design cutting pipeline stalls by 86%.
Concurrent CUDA Core + Tensor Core NTT kernel achieving throughput superior to either unit individually.
Up to 2.12x intra-ciphertext parallelism improvement without ciphertext batching; 13.4x NTT and 3.5x homomorphic multiplication speedup over TensorFHE on A100.

metrics.speedup: 13.4x NTT throughput, 3.5x homomorphic multiplication, 2.8x FHE workload vs TensorFHE on A100
metrics.other: 1218 KOPS NTT, 305 KOPS homomorphic multiplication on A100; 73% instruction reduction; 86% pipeline stall reduction

limitations: Evaluation is on A100 only; generality to newer GPU architectures (H100, B200) with different Tensor Core ISAs is not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU kernel optimization for Fully Homomorphic Encryption via concurrent CUDA and Tensor Core execution
